title: Simulation-Driven Approach for Occlusion-Based Non-Line-Of-Sight Detection Using a Low-Cost Flash LiDAR
summary: A model trained on photon patterns generated by a Monte Carlo simulator achieved 86.67% accuracy and 0.95 average precision on 180 physical measurements from a low-cost flash LiDAR for occluded-target detection. This supports an initial experimental sensing result, not general hidden-scene reconstruction.
ai_technology: Simulation-trained neural network for flash-LiDAR sensing

evidence.tested: A model trained on photon patterns generated by a Monte Carlo simulator achieved 86.67% accuracy and 0.95 average precision on 180 physical measurements from a low-cost flash LiDAR for occluded-target detection. evidence.unknown: The study evaluates the reported models and datasets only; broader generalization and real-world deployment outcomes were not established.
evidence.ai_role: A learned model detects multi-bounce photon patterns associated with hidden targets; synthetic Monte Carlo data were used for training before evaluation on physical flash-LiDAR measurements.
